company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, which goes by Stanford HAI, is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and based in Stanford, California. Its site says it advances AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition, and it describes human-centered AI as an approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being throughout the development and deployment of AI systems. Fei-Fei Li and John Etchemendy are named as Denning Co-Directors. Etchemendy's stated view is that the field spans the entire university and requires the full range of disciplinary expertise. Li describes a historical opportunity and responsibility to establish a human-centered framework for AI research, education, practice, and policy.

The institute's own account of its work covers fellowship programs for researchers working at intersections overlooked by traditional departments, grant programs, affinity groups for students, courses for leaders and decision-makers, specialized training for policymakers and civil servants, and work with the K-12 ecosystem. Its policy work is described as evidence-based research and global convenings. It publishes an annual AI Index, which the site says reveals a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared institutions are to manage it, and notes declining data transparency. Other items on the site include a research finding that users with limited social networks who seek emotional support from AI companions experience lower well-being, and Clinical Mind AI, described as a Stanford-developed international collaborative platform that uses AI-simulated patient encounters to strengthen clinical reasoning education across health professions. Erik Brynjolfsson, director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab and a senior fellow at Stanford HAI, argues that businesses can return larger gains by using AI for employees' productivity than by replacing workers. The site also notes that the Joint California Summit on Generative AI was highlighted in Governor Newsom's Executive Order.

The profile records no litigation cases, no tracked products, and no MCP servers for the institute. Its law exposure is recorded in California, with a count of 281.
